narrative.title: The Skyscraper Column Census
narrative.scenario: A skyline model arranges buildings as a binary tree: each building sits one floor below its parent, with children slotted one column left and one column right. The city surveyor photographs the model from directly above and reads each column top to bottom. When two buildings share a column and floor, the readout lists them in ascending identifier order — no exceptions, even if construction order says otherwise.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child. The root is at column 0 and row 0.
narrative.outputFormat: Return a list of lists: columns ordered left to right, each column's values sorted by row, then by value for ties.

testCases.explanation: Column -1 holds 9; column 0 reads 3 above 15; columns 1 and 2 hold 20 and 7.
Column 0 lists 1 (row 0) before 5 and 6 (row 2), which tie by row.

hintLevels: Level 1: Assign coordinates — children shift one column away from the root and one row down.
Level 2: Sweep level by level so rows come out in order naturally, parking (row, value) pairs per column.
Level 3: Emit columns in sorted key order, sorting each column's pairs by (row, value) so same-cell collisions break by value.
